The part of a living thing that carries genetic information.
The fundamental nature or values of a person, or an organization or other thing, especially when considered as innate or immutable.

The monomer constituting DNA or RNA biopolymer molecules. Each nucleotide consists of a nitrogenous heterocyclic base (or nucleobase), which can be either a double-ringed purine or a single-ringed pyrimidine; a five-carbon pentose sugar (deoxyribose in DNA or ribose in RNA); and a phosphate group.

A derivative of the pentose sugar ribose in which the 2' hydroxyl (-OH) is reduced to a hydrogen (H); it is a constituent of the nucleotides that constitute the biopolymer, deoxyribonucleic acid, or DNA.
A set of two nucleotides on opposite complementary DNA or RNA strands that are connected with hydrogen bonds.
A base, C₅H₅N₅, found in certain glands and tissues, which pairs with thymine in DNA and uracil in RNA.
A heterocyclic base, 5-methylpyrimidine-2,4(1H,3H)-dione; it pairs with adenine in DNA.
A substance first obtained from guano; it is a nucleic base and pairs with cytosine in DNA and RNA (by means of three hydrogen bonds).
A heterocyclic base, 4-aminopyrimidin-2(1H)-one, which pairs with guanine in DNA and RNA (by means of three hydrogen bonds).
The Y-shaped region of a chromosome that is the site of DNA replication
An enzyme that assists DNA replication.
An enzyme required for DNA unwinding.
Any of a group of enzymes that catalyze the binding of two molecules; synthetase.

A prayer or devotional book intended for laity, initially an abridgment of the breviary and manual including the hours of the Virgin Mary, 15 gradual and 7 penitential psalms, the litany, the placebo and dirige forming the office of the dead, and the commendations.
Any of various similar works issued in England for private prayer in accordance with the Book of Common Prayer.
A children's book intended to teach literacy: how to read, write, and spell.
An introductory text on any subject, particularly basic concepts.
An elementary school class; an elementary school student.
Any substance or device, such as priming wire or blasting cap, used to ignite gunpowder or other explosive.
A person who primes explosives.
A substance used to prime wood, metal, etc. in preparation for painting.
A layer of such a substance.
A layer of makeup that goes beneath the foundation; undermakeup.
A person who primes wood, metal, etc.
A molecule which initiates the synthesis of an enzyme, (especially) a single-stranded nucleic acid molecule which initiates DNA replication.
A pheromone which interacts first with the endocrine system.
A device used to prime an internal combustion engine with gasoline, (especially) in airplanes.
A person who prunes trees.
First in time, initial, early.
First in importance, premier.
First in position, foremost.
A surname.
The strand of DNA that is synthesized during replication
The strand of DNA that is replicated from the 5' to the 3' direction.
One of many short, newly synthesized DNA fragments formed on the lagging template strand (i.e. lagging strand) during DNA replication.
The noncoding strand of a DNA molecule that is used as a template for RNA synthesis
A weak bond in which a hydrogen atom in one molecule is attracted to an electronegative atom (usually nitrogen or oxygen) in the same or different molecule.
To bond to another species by means of hydrogen bonds. E.g. Water hydrogen bonds with itself.
A method for the separation of biological macromolecules such as protein or nucleic acids
The string of base pairs (adenine, thymine, cytosine, and guanine) which, when arranged in triplets to form codons, create a DNA string which encodes polypeptides.
Having two strands.
That have two helical strands of nucleic acid that wind around each other and are connected by hydrogen bonds.
Having one strand.
